favourite.heading: Why Minnesota can pull away
bullets: Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 9.7 points to Minnesota (+9.7 pts).

Minnesota is the better football team by 4.3 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+4.3 pts).
Playing at Minnesota is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Minnesota by 1.4 points: ball control vs front disruption (+1.4 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Akron can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -3.6 to p90 +40.4 for Minnesota, so a projection of +19.4 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.

The market disagrees by 9.1 points. The market is not the truth, but a gap that large is more often the model missing information (a suspension, a starter, a scheme change) than the market being wrong.
